title: Teach kaizen to sharpen rules from the overrides builds leave behind
summary: Until now kaizen could only seed a project's packs and wait for instructions. Six days of real deliveries showed how pack rules actually fail: the enforced wording drops the condition that says when the rule applies, builders override it, and a human patches the pack later. This turns on the second phase the original design promised: new rules must carry their condition in the enforced wording, repeated overrides with a shared reason trigger a narrow, evidence-cited sharpening, anything that would loosen a rule becomes an erosion note for the human instead, and every edit lands where pack provenance allows — never in a seeded cache. The how-to guide moves sharpening from coming soon to here, so consumers read what actually runs.
motivation: The override markers builds leave behind are a real signal that a rule overreaches, and today nothing processes them; meanwhile mislabeled fix commits are invisible to the bench that measures kaizen. Activating sharpening with a tight threshold, a one-way direction rule, and explicit surface rules turns that signal into reviewed pack improvements without ever letting kaizen weaken a gate.

included: agents/karta-kaizen.md — retire the phase-one disclaimers that stop being true, add the first-draft scoping discipline, the sharpening pass, the surface-resolution rules, the pinned commit label, and the widened run envelope
skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md — the same activation mirrored in the orchestrating skill: the dispatch carries the sharpening pass, the phase wording updates, and the envelope slots are named
The regenerated projections of both canonical files — the Codex agent file, the references copies of the agent, and the skill mirrors — kept generated-identical by the sync scripts in the same change
docs/how-to/kaizen.md — sharpening, erosion notes, surface resolution, and the commit label discipline documented as active behavior; the coming-soon section shrinks to phase three only
excluded: Phase three stays out: new-pack suggestions and the advisory/enforcing pack flag with its gate mechanics remain a later phase, still labeled as coming
The bench auditor and the field-health probe are not edited — they are the measuring sticks this work is graded by
No hook changes and no validate_packs.py changes — this is doctrine and docs only, with no new enforcement machinery and no validator schema change
No built-in pack content changes — the discipline governs how kaizen edits a consumer repo's packs, not what karta's shipped packs say
No migrations in consumer repos — resolving existing divergent packs elsewhere (for example the gringotts overlays) is follow-on work that uses these shapes, not part of this binder

The commit-trailer enforcement hook the review panel cut stays cut — evidence discipline is doctrine, reviewable in every commit and measurable by a future bench probe if coverage slips, not a new mechanism

work_items.title: Turn on the sharpening pass in kaizen's own instructions
work_items.summary: Both canonical kaizen files stop disclaiming sharpening and start defining it: when a rule may be sharpened, where the edit lands, what evidence it must carry, and what happens when the signal points toward loosening. The generated projections re-sync in the same change.
work_items.contract: Edit the two canonical kaizen doctrine files — agents/karta-kaizen.md and skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md — then regenerate their projections; never hand-edit a mirror. (1) RETIRE the phase-one disclaimers where they stop being true, in every named location: in agents/karta-kaizen.md the frontmatter `description` phase sentence ('Phase one ships the frame only — sharpening rules and suggesting new packs arrive in later phases'), the '**This is phase one: the frame.**' paragraph, the 'Editing a pack' opening sentence ('Beyond seeding, phase one gives you no signal to act on by yourself'), and the '**Phase-one honesty.**' rule; in skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md the frontmatter `description` phase sentence, the '**This is phase one: the frame.**' paragraph, the Phase 3 dispatch sentence ('Beyond seeding, phase one edits a pack only on a concrete instruction carried in the dispatch'), and the '**Phase-one honesty.**' rule. Each replacement states that sharpening, erosion notes, and the first-draft discipline are active, while phase 3 — new-pack suggestions and the advisory/enforcing pack flag with its gate mechanics — remains explicitly a later phase. The honesty rule's replacement is pinned verbatim, byte-identical in both files: '**Phase-two honesty.** Sharpening, erosion notes, and the first-draft discipline are live; new-pack suggestions and the advisory/enforcing pack flag are not built yet — never pretend to them: when a run has nothing it can do within phase two, say so in the envelope and stop.' Section placement is pinned: in agents/karta-kaizen.md the first-draft discipline and the sharpening pass land in the 'Editing a pack' section, the envelope slots in the report/envelope section, and the direction rule restated under Rules; in skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md the sharpening pass lands in the kaizen:write phase step, the envelope slots in the report step, and the direction rule under Rules. After the edit NONE of these phase-one strings appears in either canonical file: 'not active yet', 'This is phase one', 'Phase one ships the frame only', 'phase one gives you no signal', 'phase one edits a pack only on'. (2) ADD the first-draft scoping discipline for new and repaired rules: the enforced checklist wording must itself name the observable condition under which the rule applies — a condition stated only in Do/Don't/Patterns prose does not count. Mandate carve-out: a checklist mandate is reserved for rules whose violation is deterministically observable in a diff; a lesson without such a signature lands as advisory guidance with a decision procedure (a stated when-to-apply condition the builder can evaluate); single-incident lessons default to advisory. Counterexample scan: before landing a new rule, kaizen scans the repo for sites the drafted wording would flag and attaches the site list to the commit body as evidence for the reviewer — never an auto-gate. New and sharpened rules cite provenance inline in the form (seen <date>, <delivery> delivery). (3) ADD the sharpening pass to delivery mode, running after the existing seed/migrate work: read the blast radius for new KARTA-SME-OVERRIDE markers and tally standing markers repo-wide per rule id (markers use the karta-build 6-sme grammar, KARTA-SME-OVERRIDE(<rule-id>): <rationale> — reference it, do not redefine it). Threshold: two or more occurrences sharing a reason across two or more distinct deliveries sharpen the rule (the narrow, evidence-cited exception); a single occurrence is recorded as a candidate in the run envelope and commit body only; an explicit concrete instruction carried in the dispatch — the same dispatch-instruction mechanism phase one already defines — may still sharpen from a single occurrence. Direction rule: a sharper or clarifying change kaizen writes; anything that would loosen becomes an erosion note instead — rule id, override count, the builds (delivery slugs), the reasons given, and what loosening would let through — recorded in the run envelope and the kaizen commit body ONLY, never in a pack. Stale-exclusion re-check, on each sharpening pass: compare each standing replacement rule whose text begins 'Narrows <built-in-id>:' against the current built-in text; when upstream has absorbed the narrowing, propose retiring the exclusion as an envelope note, never as an autonomous edit. (4) ADD the surface-resolution rules for where a sharpening lands: a built-in rule with a repo-specific lesson lands in the repo's EXISTING project pack, via exclude_rules on the built-in id plus a replacement rule under the project prefix whose text begins 'Narrows <built-in-id>:'; a built-in rule with an environment-generic lesson becomes an upstream candidate note in the envelope and commit body (promotion into the built-in stays a human act in the karta repo); a rule in the repo's own project pack is edited in place, subject to the same direction rule — a would-loosen change to a project-pack rule becomes an erosion note, never an edit; a seeded cache never — kaizen never edits a seeded cache in place; kaizen NEVER creates a project pack — when sharpening needs one that does not exist, it emits the proposed scaffold (frontmatter plus the replacement rule) in its envelope for a human to create; in karta's own dogfood repo the house pack is edited in place and the managed byte-identical minimalism shadow never. (5) PIN the commit label: the commit subject prefix is exactly 'kaizen: ' — the form the bench auditor measures — and the 'kaizen(<pack>):' variants are documented as non-conforming. (6) UNCHANGED and restated: the never-weaken core rule, writer confinement (.karta/sme/ plus .karta/kaizen.json, hook-enforced), and the envelope-shaped report all stay; the envelope gains named slots — candidates, erosion_notes, upstream_candidates, proposed_scaffolds — defined in the agent's envelope/report section and named in the skill's report step, so both canonical files carry the same slot names; doctrine text only, no code. (7) MIRRORED SURFACE: skills/ and agents/ are canonical. After editing, run python3 scripts/sync_codex_agents.py and python3 scripts/sync_codex_skills.py so .codex/agents/karta-kaizen.toml, skills/karta-kaizen/references/karta-kaizen.agent.md, .agents/skills/karta-kaizen/references/karta-kaizen.agent.md, plugins/karta/skills/karta-kaizen/references/karta-kaizen.agent.md, .agents/skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md, and plugins/karta/skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md stay generated-identical; python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test fails otherwise.

oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; for f in agents/karta-kaizen.md skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md; do for s in "Narrows <built-in-id>:" "never edits a seeded cache in place" "two or more distinct deliveries" "(seen <date>, <delivery> delivery)" "upstream candidate" "erosion note" "Phase-two honesty."; do grep -qF -- "$s" "$f"; done; for n in "not active yet" "This is phase one" "Phase one ships the frame only" "phase one gives you no signal" "phase one edits a pack only on"; do if grep -qF -- "$n" "$f"; then exit 1; fi; done; done' && python3 scripts/sync_codex_agents.py --check && python3 scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check && python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test
assertions: the literal string 'not active yet' appears in neither agents/karta-kaizen.md nor skills/karta-kaizen/SKILL.md, and every named phase-one disclaimer location — both frontmatter descriptions, both 'This is phase one: the frame.' paragraphs, the agent's 'Editing a pack' opening, the skill's Phase 3 dispatch sentence, and both 'Phase-one honesty' rules — is rewritten so sharpening and erosion notes read as active while new-pack suggestions and the advisory/enforcing flag stay a later phase

both canonical files state the first-draft discipline: the enforced checklist wording names its observable applicability condition (prose-only conditions do not count), mandates are reserved for diff-observable violations with single-incident lessons defaulting to advisory with a decision procedure, the counterexample site list is commit-body evidence never an auto-gate, and provenance is cited inline as (seen <date>, <delivery> delivery)

both canonical files define the delivery-mode sharpening pass after seed/migrate: new markers read from the blast radius, standing markers tallied repo-wide per rule id, the threshold of two or more occurrences sharing a reason across two or more distinct deliveries, a single occurrence recorded as an envelope candidate only, dispatch-instructed sharpening from one still allowed, and the stale-exclusion re-check proposing retirements as envelope notes

the direction rule holds in both files: sharper or clarifying is written; anything loosening becomes an erosion note (rule id, override count, builds, reasons, what loosening would let through) in the run envelope and kaizen commit body only, never in a pack

the surface-resolution rules land in both files: the existing project pack with exclude_rules plus a 'Narrows <built-in-id>:' replacement for repo-specific lessons, upstream candidate notes for environment-generic lessons, project-pack rules edited in place, kaizen never edits a seeded cache in place, kaizen never creates a project pack and instead emits the proposed scaffold in its envelope, and the karta dogfood row (house pack in place, minimalism shadow never)
the commit label is pinned to the exact subject prefix 'kaizen: ' with the 'kaizen(<pack>):' variants documented as non-conforming

the never-weaken core rule, writer confinement, and the envelope report survive unchanged, and the envelope gains named slots for candidates, erosion notes, upstream candidates, and proposed scaffolds

sync_codex_agents.py --check and sync_codex_skills.py --check both report no drift across the .codex toml, the references copies, and the skill mirrors, and validate_plugin --self-test passes with all [PASS]

work_items.title: Move sharpening from coming soon to here in the kaizen guide
work_items.summary: Readers of the kaizen how-to learn what the sharpening pass actually does now — the threshold, the direction rule, where edits land, and the exact commit label — and the coming-soon list shrinks to the one phase still ahead.
work_items.contract: docs/how-to/kaizen.md only. Move rule sharpening and erosion notes out of the 'What's coming' section into active documentation: describe what the sharpening pass does on every delivery run (reads new KARTA-SME-OVERRIDE markers in the blast radius and tallies standing markers per rule id), the threshold (two or more occurrences sharing a reason across two or more distinct deliveries sharpen the rule; a single occurrence is recorded as a candidate only), and the direction rule (a sharper or clarifying change kaizen writes; anything that would loosen becomes an erosion note showing the rule, the override count, the reasons given, and what loosening would let through — and erosion notes live in the kaizen commit body and the run envelope, never in a pack). Document the surface-resolution rules for a consumer: kaizen never edits a seeded cache in place; sharpening a built-in rule lands in the repo's existing project pack as an exclusion plus a replacement rule whose text begins 'Narrows <built-in-id>:'; an environment-generic lesson becomes an upstream candidate note for karta's maintainers rather than a local edit; kaizen never creates the project pack — it proposes the scaffold in its envelope and a human creates it. Document the evidence citation readers will see inside sharpened rules — (seen <date>, <delivery> delivery) — and the label discipline: kaizen's commits carry the exact subject prefix 'kaizen: ', and the 'kaizen(<pack>):' variants are non-conforming. 'What's coming' retains ONLY phase 3: new-pack suggestions and the advisory mechanics that let a drafted pack guide builders without gating builds. Plain language throughout per the karta-plainlanguage standard; every canonical term above stays byte-identical to the doctrine files from the sharpening-doctrine item — the shared_terms gate holds them — and the doc-truth parity binding must stay coherent (no promise the repo does not keep, no phase label that contradicts the doctrine). Additionally add ONE doc-truth claims row to benchmarks/claims.yaml, id 'KAIZEN-LABEL-PARITY', in the probe's existing check vocabulary, binding the guide's pinned label promise to the bench auditor's measuring regex: the doc promises the exact subject prefix 'kaizen: ' and the row asserts benchmarks/field/audit_companions.py still anchors its kaizen-commit regex to that prefix — so a future auditor change flags the doc instead of silently orphaning it. The row must make the live parity probe pass; the probe file itself is never edited.

oracle.command: sh -c 'set -e; for s in "Narrows <built-in-id>:" "never edits a seeded cache in place" "two or more distinct deliveries" "(seen <date>, <delivery> delivery)" "upstream candidate" "erosion note"; do grep -qF -- "$s" docs/how-to/kaizen.md; done' && grep -q 'KAIZEN-LABEL-PARITY' benchmarks/claims.yaml && python3 benchmarks/probes/parity-doc-truth-ledger.py --target . | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);sys.exit(0 if d['status']=='pass' else 1)" && python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test

the doc states erosion notes live in the kaizen commit body and the run envelope, never in a pack

the surface-resolution rules are documented for a consumer: kaizen never edits a seeded cache in place, sharpening lands in the existing project pack with a 'Narrows <built-in-id>:' replacement, environment-generic lessons become an upstream candidate note, and kaizen never creates the project pack but proposes its scaffold for a human to create

the label discipline is documented — the exact subject prefix 'kaizen: ' with the 'kaizen(<pack>):' variants called non-conforming — and the evidence citation form (seen <date>, <delivery> delivery) is shown
